featured_reviews.name: Jahnavi Bhosle
featured_reviews.review_text: Terrible experience. We ordered Puri and bhaji and when we tasted it, we told them the food was bland, the bhaji did not have any salt and neither did the puri. Firstly, our server didn't make it clear about the portions of the dish. Then the puri bhaji was very bland, it felt like eating water. The guy was far too busy arguing with us how the puri is fine, "we purposely put less salt in case the bhaji is spicy/salty". He was busy advocating how we're wrong, and that the whole dish is not bland, only the bhaji, we'll replace the bhaji not the puri (after taking it to the kitchen already). We were trying to enjoy the food and the guy was just munching out our head as if he's a lawyer tryna prove his case to us. Finally he's like what do we do, at that point we didn't even wanna eat at their place anymore. He started insisting cancel the dish then, as if he's lending us a favour by feeding us. The chef gave us a new order with the bhaji and puri newly made and properly seasoned. But such terrible staff manners and immense unprofessionalism. Three men were just standing at my booth arguing with me while I eat!!!??? I'm here to eat food not fight, bullshit!

featured_reviews.name: Bhagyashree Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Taste of Kerala in Fort and absolutely loved the experience. The restaurant serves authentic Kerala-style food and everything we ordered was delicious.

We tried Chicken Chettinad, Chicken 65, and another chicken starter (don’t remember the name), and all of them were extremely tasty. The Chicken 65 was quite different from the usual version we get it had a unique Kerala-style flavor which made it even better.

They also serve complimentary curries, pickle, mirchi, papad, and a salad made with onion, amla, and mango in a vinegar-style dressing. Even these sides were so flavorful and really added to the meal.

Overall, the food was amazing and satisfying. If you enjoy Kerala cuisine, this place is definitely a must-try.

featured_reviews.name: ZARIF AHMAD
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited The Taste of Kerala and honestly, I loved the experience.The Chicken Taste of Malabar was rich and full of flavor, with perfectly cooked chicken. The Chicken Kizhi Biryani was aromatic and delicious - you can really taste the authentic Kerala spices. The Chicken Kizhi Parotta was soft, well-layered , and very satisfying. My favorite was the Chicken Chettinad Boneless - spicy , flavorful, and cooked just right .Overall, everything tasted fresh and authentic . Definitely a place I’d visit again !

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text: Decent family apt ambience, good selection of Kerala menu, authentic taste and reasonably priced items. Family as well as friends can visit. We ordered Kadala curry (black gram curry), veg stew, idiyappam, Kerala wheat parotta, and veg korma. We also got complimentary payasam for dessert. Over all, good experience. I would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Saurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered veg biryani from Taste of Kerala on 13 October 2025, but I was delivered chicken biryani instead. This is a serious issue, especially for someone who does not eat non-veg.
I immediately went to the restaurant and showed them the delivered order. They said the owner was not present and asked me to return the food and come back the next day for a refund. I trusted them and handed over the food.
When I returned the next day, the owner refused to take responsibility and told me to contact Zomato instead. This was extremely unprofessional and dishonest.
This is not just a mistake—it’s a serious concern when non-veg food is served while claiming it is veg. Please be very careful. If the intention was to avoid a refund, they could have been honest instead of wasting my time.
I do not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Rituka Nakhawa
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Taste of Kerala and had a really good experience overall. The place serves tasty, authentic food with nice service. Due to the crowd, the staff does struggle a bit with serving everyone on time, but they still manage with a positive attitude.
We tried the Sunday Special Veg Banana Meal, Coconut Chilly Roasted Chicken with Kerala Paratha, and Chicken Kizhi Parotha. Every dish was absolutely delicious — rich flavours and true Kerala taste. We’ll definitely be visiting again!
A special mention to the manager, who was extremely warm and attentive. He personally checked on every table, and when he noticed we enjoyed the payasam, he even served us some extra. Such gestures really make the experience memorable. 💛🌴✨

review_photos.caption: Roasted coconut chilly chicken with Kerala parotha

featured_reviews.name: Hozefa Topiwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Taste of Kerala is truly a hidden gem! The place has a simple, no-frills setup — the ground floor is non-AC while the mezzanine floor is AC, though the ceiling upstairs is a bit low and seating is quite basic. But once the food arrives, you forget everything else!

The service here is absolutely fantastic. We were served by Raki, who was super enthusiastic and guided us through the menu with genuine passion. The restaurant is really lucky to have such a dedicated person on their team.

We ordered Chicken Pachamolak, Chicken Kerala, and Prawn Ghee Roast with wheat Laccha Kerala Paratha, and every dish was lip-smacking delicious. The authentic Kerala flavors were spot on!

They also serve complimentary Kerala papad, dahi boondi salad, and a variety of authentic chutneys, which are a must-try and perfectly complement the meal.

Overall, an amazing experience — fantastic food, warm service, and great value for money. We’ll definitely be visiting again and again!

featured_reviews.name: ittyadee bal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The menu shows a Veg Thali for ₹350, but on Sunday we were charged ₹440 for a “Sunday Special Thali.” The server did not inform us beforehand that the ₹350 thali was not available on Sundays. Only after we finished eating did he mention this.

It would have been better if this was clearly communicated before ordering. Also, the thali didn’t feel particularly “special” to justify the higher price. Transparency with customers would improve the experience.

featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the benne dosa at Madras Mood Cafe and it was absolutely delicious! Perfectly crispy on the outside, soft inside, and rich with buttery flavor. Definitely a must-try if you love authentic South Indian food. Will be coming back for more!

featured_reviews.name: Zoya Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I really wanted to try some dosa with chicken curry and hence I visited this place. But to my disappointment, they stopped serving non-vegetarian items and the place is now 100% vegetarian. That was a bummer.

Speaking of food their benne masala dosa was delicious. It was crispy, with a kick of gunpowder on the inside and the potato filling was good. The two chutneys paired really well with the dosa. Also, another disappointment was that they don’t serve Sambar.

Their medu vada and their ghee podi thatte idli was okay. I ordered a filter coffee which was pre-made version. Nonetheless it was chilled and had a nice taste.

I would so recommend this place just for their pocket friendly benne dosa.

Maybe I gotta visit their other outlets to try their non-vegetarian options.

Bhagat Tarachand is a vegetarian, air-conditioned restaurant with comfortable seating and a lively yet pleasant ambience. They serve Punjabi cuisine and offer Jain options as well. The place is well known for serving hot, fresh food consistently, which really elevates the dining experience.

One of their highlights is the signature chaas served in a beer bottle, which is chilled, refreshing, and pairs perfectly with the meal. Overall food quality is excellent, with rich flavours and generous portions.

Overall, almost everything on the menu tastes amazing, making it a reliable spot for satisfying vegetarian Punjabi food.

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji – A Legendary Spot for Classic Pav Bhaji Lovers

Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is a well-known name among street food lovers, especially for those who enjoy rich, buttery, and authentic Mumbai-style Pav Bhaji. Over the years, this place has built a strong reputation for consistent taste, generous portions, and a no-nonsense approach to food. It is a go-to destination for locals and visitors who want to enjoy comforting Indian street food without unnecessary frills.

The highlight here is undoubtedly the Pav Bhaji. The bhaji is thick, flavorful, and perfectly mashed, cooked on a large iron tawa with a generous amount of butter. The blend of vegetables, spices, and butter creates a rich, slightly smoky flavor that reflects the traditional street-style preparation. The spice level is well balanced, making it enjoyable for most palates, while still delivering the bold taste pav bhaji lovers expect.

The pav is soft, fresh, and well toasted with butter, complementing the bhaji beautifully. Each serving comes with chopped onions, lemon, and extra butter on top, allowing customers to customize the taste according to their preference. The consistency of the bhaji is one of the strongest points—neither too watery nor too dry—which shows the experience and skill behind its preparation.

Apart from pav bhaji, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is also popular for its dosa varieties. The dosas are crisp, well-cooked, and generously filled, making them a good alternative for those who want something different. However, pav bhaji remains the star dish that draws most of the crowd.

The ambience is simple and functional, typical of a popular street-food-style eatery. Seating is basic, but the focus here is clearly on food quality rather than décor. Despite the constant rush, the place is usually clean, and food preparation can be seen openly, which builds trust among customers.

Service is quick and efficient. Orders are taken promptly, and food is served hot without long waiting times, even during peak hours. The staff is experienced and handles the crowd well, ensuring a smooth flow despite the popularity of the place.

Pricing is reasonable and offers good value for money considering the portion size and taste. Compared to many modern cafés serving pav bhaji at premium prices, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji delivers authentic flavor at a fair cost, making it accessible to everyone.

Historically, places like Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji represent the true spirit of Indian street food culture—simple ingredients, skilled cooking, and a loyal customer base built over years of trust. Many regular customers associate this place with late-night cravings, family outings, and food memories that bring people back again and again.

Overall, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is a must-visit for anyone who truly appreciates classic pav bhaji. It offers rich taste, consistent quality, quick service, and a nostalgic street-food experience. If you are craving buttery, flavorful pav bhaji that stays true to its roots, this place will not disappoint. 🌶️🧈

featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya – A Timeless Taste of Authentic Gujarati Thali

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is one of the most iconic and beloved places to experience authentic Gujarati cuisine. Known for its traditional thali, warm hospitality, and consistent quality, this legendary eatery has earned a special place in the hearts of locals as well as visitors. Dining here feels less like eating at a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a Gujarati household.

The moment you enter Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya, you are greeted with simplicity and warmth. The interiors are modest, clean, and functional, reflecting the traditional values of Gujarati culture where food quality and hospitality matter more than luxury décor. The seating arrangement is organized, and despite the heavy rush during peak hours, the staff manages the crowd efficiently.

The highlight, without any doubt, is the Gujarati Thali. The thali is a wholesome and balanced meal that represents the true essence of Gujarat’s culinary heritage. It usually includes a variety of rotating dishes such as shaak (vegetable curries), kadhi, dal, rotli or puri, rice, khichdi, farsan, chutneys, pickles, and traditional sweets like shrikhand or mohanthal. Each item is freshly prepared and served hot.

One of the most impressive aspects of Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is the unlimited serving system. The staff continuously serves food with great attentiveness, ensuring that guests never feel rushed or restricted. The flavors are authentic—mildly spiced, well-balanced, and comforting—making the food suitable for all age groups. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods is clearly reflected in the taste.

Historically, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya has been serving Gujarati food for decades and is considered a cultural landmark. It has preserved the original style of Gujarati dining, where meals are meant to nourish both the body and the soul. Many regular visitors associate the place with nostalgia, family gatherings, and cultural pride.

Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained throughout the restaurant. Plates, serving areas, and dining spaces are kept tidy, even during peak hours. The staff is polite, disciplined, and well trained, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience.

The pricing is reasonable, especially considering the quality, quantity, and authenticity of the food served. It offers excellent value for money and is often recommended as a must-visit place for anyone wanting to experience true Gujarati cuisine.

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya attracts a diverse crowd—families, elderly guests, tourists, and food lovers from across India. Despite the popularity and long waiting times during weekends, the management ensures smooth operations and quick table turnover without compromising service quality.

Overall, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is not just a restaurant but a celebration of Gujarati tradition, flavors, and hospitality. If you want to experience a soulful Gujarati thali prepared with authenticity and served with warmth, this place is an absolute must-visit. It leaves you with a satisfied heart, a happy stomach, and a deep appreciation for Gujarat’s rich culinary culture.

The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

featured_reviews.review_text:
AC hall has just 7 tables in total. We had to wait for 15mins waiting for a table. The low height of the roof surely makes walking tough for taller people (>6ft), becomes a little cramped up restaurant. Thankfully Indians aren’t that tall on average, so it’s manageable.
Coming to the food, since we didn’t want a long wait time we went with Special Thali while costs around Rs 450/-, the good thing being you can share the food. Thali was quite good, though others were going for ala-carte. The dal in thali was something special, never had seen so much of fried onions on top of dal. That’s what makes their dal thick and tasty. We also ordered Rabri and Lassi which was very thick, creamy, flavourful and worth the money paid for. The restaurant is located in the busy streets of Zaveri Bazaar (well known for 1993 Mumbai Blasts), so driving a private car is out of the question. Cabs are very difficult to get by.
